rule.description: A function embeds a working copy of another live function's top-level body (statement-multiset containment between functions that both still exist), or a function whose body is far larger than every ordinary function in the same crate, indicating several levels of copied-in sub-implementation.
rule.note: Implemented as a Dylint rule library run through the dylint rustc workspace-wrapper driver during cargo check of the cargo-afl targets. Statement identity is normalized (bindings and constants collapsed, call-target identities compared as symbols, literal spans compared verbatim) so renames, variable reordering, and formatting do not defeat detection, while genuinely different control flow or built-in usage does not match.

checks.description: Detect a function that contains an inlined working copy of the complete top-level body of another live function in the same crate, while the original function still exists.
checks.detected_relation: inlining function -> inlined copy of a still-live function's body
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Several levels of calls were collapsed by copying the called bodies into one caller; the copies diverge at knee-jerk variable boundaries while the originals stay behind, so the duplicated implementation must now be maintained in two places at once.

matches.evidence: main embeds a copy of the body of the startup AFL++ version probe (returns Option<String>, a probe-formulation of the same Command/stdout parsing steps) close to verbatim.
main embeds a copy of the body of the AFL++ update notice routine (network probe plus version key comparison, reformulated with let-else bindings instead of the original's plain bindings).
the cargo driver loop embeds a copy of the body of the LLVM plugin flag assembly routine (the -Z llvm-plugins rustflag accumulation loop over plugin passes) instead of delegating to it.
config embeds a copy of the body of the rustc toolchain label derivation (versionMeta probe, "rustc-" string assembly, short commit hash suffix).
config embeds a copy of the body of the package label derivation ("afl.rs-" prefix plus the compile-time package version string, including the emptiness assertion).
plugins_installed embeds a copy of the body of the same rustc toolchain label derivation that config embeds; two copies of identical label logic now exist in one crate.
plugins_installed embeds a copy of the body of the package label derivation and subsequently resolves the afl-llvm runtime directory inline instead of through the crate's path helpers.

checks.description: Detect a single function whose body is an order of magnitude larger than every ordinary function compiled in the same crate, which multi-level inlining inevitably produces; this fires even when every matched partner function has been deleted, so removing the originals is not a valid repair for this check.
checks.detected_relation: single function -> order-of-magnitude oversized body that composes several sub-implementation levels
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The method absorbed multiple levels of calls; the remaining body is too large to reason about and cannot be decomposed without re-deriving every copied-in responsibility.

matches.evidence: config carries toolchain labeling, directory resolution, repository update, build orchestration, the runtime object installation, and plugin copying in one continuous body.
main now performs AFL++ version discovery, command decoration, argument dispatch, update noticing, toolchain labeling, and runtime object resolution with inline exit logic.
run_cargo absorbs labeling, plugin directory creation, plugin presence scanning, plugin flag assembly, and the runtime link-arg plumbing in addition to its original cargo-rerouting responsibilities.

excluded.description: The still-live functions whose bodies were copied (the version/label and path helpers, the version probe, the update notice, and the plugin flag assembly) are counterpart sources of the relation, not smell locations in themselves; they are intended to remain present as the delegation targets of a repair.

Test-only modules (the clap subcommand help tests, the update/crates_io tests), the afl crate (not part of the recorded build), and cargo-afl-common's build script are outside the analyzed compilation surface and are reconciled through them if a repair touches those pieces.

Large but genuinely cohesive bodies that do not embed another live function's top-level body (for example the argument-augmentation code generated by the clap derive macros) are below the rule thresholds and excluded by design.
